### Problem

The review's evaluation (review-eval.yml, evals/review) cannot tell a worse review from a good one on the side that matters most. Its baseline (evals/review/baseline.json) is `found: 1` of 10 cases: of ten real bugs the review found and that were fixed, the review finds again only one. A change fails the check only when it is worse by more than one case, so on the found side no change can ever fail it, and a review that finds nothing passes. On the clean side it scores 10 of 10, so the review is tested for not blocking but not for finding.

Two causes are likely and not verified: the evaluation does not review the way production does (the review of #915 noted it: a fresh clone, `--full`, no token, and a fix prompt with `pr=0`), and a case counts as found only when a finding lands in the exact hunk the fix changed.

### Scope

- Find out why the review finds 1 of 10 in the evaluation, case by case, and write it in the pull request: whether the evaluation plays the review differently from production, whether the matching of a finding to the fixed hunk is too strict, or whether the review misses them.
- The evaluation plays the review the same way production does (the same brief, the same mode, the same verification), except for what runs with secrets on a fork.
- The found side has an absolute floor in policy, not only "no worse than the baseline": a review that finds fewer than the floor fails the check, whatever the baseline.
- A new baseline from a full play after the fix, committed in the same pull request.
- Tests for each.

### Out of scope

- The review's prompts and model, unless the investigation shows they are the cause; then that is its own issue.
- The autopilot's and the Spec's evaluations.

### Acceptance criteria

- C1: Given the review that production runs today, when the evaluation plays the review set, then each case is reviewed with the same brief, mode and verification as production.
- C2: Given a change to the review that finds none of the flag cases, when the evaluation scores it, then the check fails, whatever the baseline says.
- C3: Given the pull request's description, when a person reads it, then it says for each of the 10 flag cases why the review found or did not find it.

### Criticality

Critical
